relevance_note: The paper describes four named family members carrying a TNFAIP3 frameshift variant: "A heterozygous c.1727dupC variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (NM_006290), introducing the frameshift variant p.His577Alafs*95, was identified in the Pt1 and her mother (Pt 4)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values I typed and checked every span verbatim. Labels: the text introduces 'Patient N (PtN)' and uses 'PtN' most often; Table 1 prints 'Pt N' in a merged label cell that the converter repeats on every row, so 'Pt1'-'Pt4' were used. Table 1 has patients as rows (one row per manifestation); table spans quote from the 'Pt N' label through the cell. Scope: the four carriers (Pt1-Pt4) plus Pt1's father, who was sequenced with Pt1 ('Pt1 and her parents') and whose PBMCs/plasma were used in Figures 3-4; the paper never states his genotype or phenotype, so he has no variant row and all checklist items are 'not reported'. Recurrent fever was set 'excluded' for Pt1, Pt2 and Pt4 from the named group statement 'Only Pt3 presented with recurrent episodes of fevers in childhood.' Count-only statements (genital ulcers 'in 1 patient', chronic arthritis 2/4, thyroiditis 3/4, diabetes and hemolytic anemia 'in 1 patient', anti-thyroid antibodies in 3 of 4, pSTAT1 increased in 3 of 4) were not used to exclude anyone. For Pt3, 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14' was applied to the checklist items the paper itself lists as its autoimmune manifestations in the preceding sentence (thyroiditis, diabetes, hemolytic anemia -> autoimmune cytopenia); it was not applied to 'arthritis or arthralgia' (the paper's item is the narrower 'chronic arthritis'), autoimmune hepatitis (never mentioned) or autoantibodies (laboratory finding). Short stature in Table 1 and 'stunted growth' were mapped to the checklist item 'growth failure'. Age at onset in individuals uses Table 1 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)'; no ISO duration was given because 'less than 2 years' is an upper bound, not an age. Inheritance 'inherited maternal' for Pt1-Pt3 rests on the mother (Pt4) carrying the same heterozygous variant ('identified in the Pt1 and her mother (Pt 4)'); the paper does not use the word 'inherited'. Pt4's anti-TG value (77 U/ml) is below the stated normal value (<100 U/ml) although listed under 'Autoantibody Positivity'; no anti-TG feature row was made for Pt4. Consanguinity left 'not reported': the abstract calls the four patients 'consanguineous', which appears to mean blood-related (a mother and her daughters), not parental consanguinity. Contradictions/inconsistencies: Pt3 is 'a 13 year-old girl' but 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14'; Pt2 short stature '3° centile for height at that time' (text) vs '3°-25° centile' (Table 1); Pt3 '3° centile' (text) vs '<3° centile' (Table 1); Pt4 adult height '10-20° centile' (text) vs 'Short stature (10-25°)' (Table 1), and the Results' 'final height below or slightly above 3rd percentile' does not fit Pt4's centile; transcript printed without version (NM_006290); the genome build GRCh37/hg19 is stated but no genomic coordinates are printed.
